summary: The wrong-828 5-token raw Graph.to_pt calibration completed. Raw graph payloads are ~0.49-0.98 GB/token for prefix lengths 73-203. Global raw top-K mass is dominated by the single logit row and reaches ~1.0 by 16k edges, confirming that global top-K/top-P is not useful for feature-feature retention. Within the selected 8192x8192 feature-feature bucket, 16k edges retain only ~31-62% mass, 100k retains ~67-90%, 500k retains ~91-99%, and 1M retains ~97-99.9%; top-P 0.95 needs ~168k-777k feature-feature edges and top-P 0.99 needs ~435k-1.84M.
interpretation: Future compact outputs should use separate edge buckets. Global top-K is dominated by logit rows; feature-feature topology needs at least ~500k edges/token for ~95% selected-feature-feature mass on these samples, or bucket top-P with a high cap around 1-2M for 0.99 coverage.

summary: Computed typed edge-bucket retention curves from the wrong-828 5-token raw Graph.to_pt calibration. Nonzero target buckets are feature<-feature, feature<-error, feature<-token, logit<-feature, logit<-error, and logit<-token; error-row and token-row target buckets are zero in this graph layout. Logit<-feature has exactly 8192 nonzero edges and can be saved all. Logit<-error and logit<-token are small and can also be saved all. Feature<-error is small enough for a 16k cap to preserve >99.6% mass. Feature<-token needs ~64k-242k edges for 95% mass. Feature<-feature remains the only million-scale bucket.

recommended_save_policy.feature<-token: top_p=0.95 with max_edges around 250k, or top_p=0.99 with max_edges around 500k
recommended_save_policy.feature<-feature: top_p=0.95 with max_edges around 1M, or top_p=0.99 with max_edges around 2M
